description: Material arriving from several trucks must keep its stream classification, issue notes, contamination flags, and handling instructions intact during handoff at a transfer site. All facilities are fictional.

user_profile.persona: 39-year-old transfer station lead overseeing a busy inbound handoff process
user_profile.context: The material moves quickly enough that classification and issue notes are at risk of being reduced to memory instead of records
user_profile.communication_style: Chain-aware and operational, wants each incoming load tied to its handling context

fact_sheet.fact: Marco Diaz is the Transfer Station Lead at the Veridian Eco-Transfer Station.
Lena Petrova is the primary Scale Operator and works at workstation Scale-01.
Kenji Tanaka is the Yard Foreman, responsible for directing trucks from the scale to the correct tipping bays.
Dr. Anya Sharma is the Regional Compliance Officer; her email is asharma@veridianeco.com.
The Veridian Eco-Transfer Station is located at 1550 Industrial Way, Port Sterling, WA 98301.
Tipping Bay 3 is exclusively designated for 'Source-Separated Organics' (SSO) streams.
Tipping Bay 5 is the designated quarantine area for any load flagged with a C-1 (Medical Waste) contamination alert.
The scale house contains two scales: Inbound Scale 1 for arriving trucks and Outbound Scale 2 for departing trucks.
Gritstone Hauling operates a fleet primarily composed of Kenworth T880 roll-off trucks.
Apex Waste Solutions truck AS-204 is equipped with an RFID tag, ID: 7A3B-9C2D-E5F6, for automated check-in.
The primary loader used for moving Construction & Demolition (C&D) material is a Caterpillar 972M Wheel Loader.
The facility uses 'StreamLine Logistics' software, accessible to staff at https://veridian.streamlinelogistics.net.
Each incoming load is assigned a unique Load ID in StreamLine Logistics, formatted as 'YYYYMMDD-XXXX'.
Contamination flags are entered into the 'Issues' field in StreamLine Logistics using codes: C-1 (Medical), C-2 (Hazardous), or C-3 (Excessive Contaminants).
All drivers from contracted haulers like Gritstone Hauling must use the 'StreamLine Driver' mobile app to log their load details before arrival.
The StreamLine Logistics system automatically archives all load records, including photos and notes, after 180 days.
A physical load ticket must be printed from the StreamLine system at Scale-01 for every inbound truck and handed to the driver.
The standard procedure for a C-2 (Hazardous) flagged load is to immediately divert it to the Hazardous Material Staging Area near Bay 6.
The handoff from the scale operator to the yard foreman is confirmed when the Load ID is posted in the '#inbound-traffic' Slack channel.
The target weigh-in-to-tip time for a standard Municipal Solid Waste (MSW) load is under 8 minutes.
As of June 1st, 2024, all C&D loads require a photographic record uploaded to their Load ID in StreamLine before tipping is authorized.
Any load with a gross weight exceeding 25 tons requires verbal or digital approval from Marco Diaz before proceeding past the scale.
'Single-Stream Recyclables' (Code: SSR) must have less than 5% contamination by weight to be accepted without a surcharge.
A C-3 flag is automatically applied by the scale operator if visible contamination in an SSR load appears to exceed 15%.
Handling instructions for any C-2 flagged load require all personnel within a 10-meter radius to wear Level C PPE.
Gritstone Hauling has a contract (Contract ID: GH-VET-2024-01) to deliver a minimum of 50 tons of C&D material daily.
On July 26, 2024, Load ID 20240726-0042 from Apex Waste Solutions was classified as MSW but flagged C-2 for containing visible car batteries.
The site's EPA Solid Waste Facility Permit number is WA-SWM-93481.
All personnel entering the tipping floor must wear a hard hat, steel-toed boots, safety glasses, and a high-visibility Class 2 vest.
A spill of more than 5 gallons of hydraulic fluid requires an immediate report to Marco Diaz and logging in the site's environmental incident log (Logbook E-11).
Urgent issues, such as a fire or a C-1 flag, require an immediate radio call to the shift supervisor on radio Channel 3.
Daily shift handoff reports are posted by the outgoing lead in the '#transfer-station-leads' Slack channel by 5 minutes past the end of their shift.
The on-duty shift supervisor's designated mobile phone number is 555-0182.
Ridgeback Environmental's truck RE-088, a front-load garbage truck, is scheduled for a 10:30 AM arrival every Tuesday with commercial MSW.
Rejected loads must be re-weighed on the outbound scale, and the reason for rejection must be selected from a dropdown menu in StreamLine Logistics before the truck is permitted to leave.
